thread:
Yuan: Nightly eval alert: structured_csv promptset failure spike after pushing v3.2.1 weights, ~2.3% drop on pass@strict. Logs attached. :eyes:
Marta: Ack — pulling logs now, can you paste one failing example?
Yuan: Here — input (trimmed):
```
PROMPT_ID: csv_042
INPUT: "id,name,score
1,ALex,0.92
2,Bea,0.78"
EXPECTED: well-formed CSV rows, no extra separators
```
OUTPUT (v3.2.1):
```
id,name,score
1,<|table|>ALex,0.92
2,Bea,0.78
```
Marta: Huh, that `<|table|>` token is new. EvalBot: nightly-eval job 2026-03-19T07:12 reported tokenization mismatch rate up from 0.1% -> 2.6% on structured_csv.
Sam: Did we change tokenizer vocab during this weight push or was it weights-only? DeployBot: Release manifest shows weights: v3.2.1, tokenizer: tokenizer-v2 (same as last deploy), but commit includes a merge from token-normalizer branch (id: 86f2).
Marta: I dumped vocab diffs vs last good (v3.1.9). Small snippet:
```
- 5019: "<|table-start|>"
+ 5019: "<|table|>"  <-- replaced
+ 5020: "<|table-start|>"  <-- inserted new id, shifts later ids
```
Marta: Looks like an off-by-one reindexing pushed a new special token in the middle. That'll shift merge/prunings and can change token boundaries for short CSV-like strings.
Yuan: Repro locally: tokenization of `ALex` prefixed by comma becomes `"," + "<|table|>ALex"` after byte-pair merge shifts. Repro command: `python -c "from tok import T; print(T.encode(',ALex'))"` shows tokens.
Sam: Good catch. Quick hypothesis: the model weights were updated with tokenizer retraining artifacts in the same release branch causing mismatch between expected merges and runtime tokenizer mapping.
EvalBot: Added failing examples to `s3://redwood-nightly-failures/2026-03-19/structured_csv/` (10 samples).
Marta: Short-term mitigation: we can force the serving stack to use the previous tokenizer artifact (tokenizer-v1.9) while we triage. That avoids id-shift until we fix the mapping.
Yuan: Agreed. Sam — can you trigger a canary rollback of tokenizer only?
Sam: I'll open a deploy ticket. Command I plan to run:
```
./deploy --service=inference --tokenizer=tokenizer-v1.9 --strategy=canary --pct=5
```
Sam: Note: need to ensure weights remain v3.2.1 — we only swap tokenizer artifact. Any objections?
Marta: No objections. Also we should run a quick ablation: weights v3.2.1 + old tokenizer vs weights v3.1.9 + old tokenizer to confirm root cause.
Yuan: I ran that locally — v3.2.1 + tokenizer-v1.9 reduces failures to baseline (0.12%), so root cause is tokenizer id shift not weights.
Sam: Canary rolled out to 5% — DeployBot: canary complete, 5% traffic now on tokenizer-v1.9. Monitoring: latency unchanged, error rate normal.
Marta: Nice. Next: create a deterministic mapping script to map the new vocab ids back to legacy ids for customers who already pulled tokenizer-v2. Also open PR to revert tokenizer merge until we ship a safe remap.
Yuan: I'll produce a token-id-translation table and a small patch to pre-process inputs for structured prompt sets (only as fallback for csv/tsv style prompts).
Marta: Also add a nightly eval that checks for special-token insertions inside ASCII punctuation-heavy prompts — alerted earlier-than regression next time.
Sam: Filed ticket INF-4721: "tokenizer merge reindex caused special-token insertion -> structured_csv failures" and linked canary logs. Assigning to Marta and Yuan.
Yuan: Taking the ticket. Plan: 1) validate full vocab diff, 2) craft id-translation table, 3) run eval/regression harness on remapped tokenizer, 4) propose final revert or safe reindex plan.
EvalBot: nightly-eval will re-run structured_csv after canary reaches 100% or rollback confirmed.
Marta: For postmortem: add notes about changing special-token insertion procedures and require end-to-end eval for structured-output promptsets before shipping tokenizer changes.
Yuan: Thanks all. Leaving logs and a few failing examples in the thread S3 link. :thumbsup:
